claims.text: High-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings is governed by a continuous, adherent, nanostructured oxide tribolayer.
The oxide tribolayer forms through selective oxidation of alloying components such as Cu or Cr.
The oxide tribolayer reduces friction by providing a lubricious sliding surface.
The oxide tribolayer impedes wear by providing a hard surface barrier.
The oxide tribolayer arrests crack initiation and propagation under sliding contact.
As-deposited FeNiCrCoCu films have a fine-grained microstructure typical of sputtered or evaporated films.
The as-deposited baseline coating has no pre-formed oxide scale.
Pre-oxidation in air at approximately 700 °C for 1 hour promotes surface oxidation before wear testing.
Pre-oxidation produces a continuous, nanocrystalline oxide layer containing Cu and/or Cr oxides.
The oxide layer reduces direct metal-to-metal contact.
At high temperature in an oxidative environment, selective oxidation produces a stable oxide tribolayer.
The oxide tribolayer is self-healing during high-temperature sliding.
The adherent oxide barrier alleviates stress concentrations and hinders coating delamination.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have significantly lower wear rates than as-deposited coatings under identical high-temperature sliding conditions.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have significantly lower friction coefficients than as-deposited coatings under identical high-temperature sliding conditions.
The treated coating will retain a uniform, intact oxide layer after wear testing.
The unoxidized baseline will exhibit more severe wear damage, spallation, or crack propagation than the pre-oxidized coating.
The proposed mechanism applies approximately from 500 to 700 °C under moderate sliding-contact loads on conventional metallic substrates.
